title: Toolkit for DNA Extraction and Library Preparation for Nanopore Sequencing
author: Inswasti Cahyani
materials: A DNA extraction protocol that yields clean and homogeneous UHMW DNA is essential for a good ultra-long (UL) sequencing output. We have routinely used the New England Biolabs (NEB) Monarch HMW DNA Extraction Kit for Cells & Blood (T3050) for UL library preparations, with the following modifications. *This protocol has been optimised in human cell lines.*
Reprime the flow cell as before.

A DNA extraction protocol that yields clean and homogeneous UHMW DNA is essential for a good ultra-long (UL) sequencing output. We have routinely used the New England Biolabs (NEB) Monarch HMW DNA Extraction Kit for Cells & Blood (T3050) for UL library preparations, with the following modifications. *This protocol has been optimised in human cell lines.*

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: For each reaction use 6 × 10⁶ human cells, pellet and wash twice with cold PBS at 7000 × g, 1 min, 4 °C (or room temperature if not specified). Ensure high viability and accurate cell count.

steps.title: Pre‑heat thermomixer
steps.instruction: Heat thermomixer to 56 °C, 700 rpm. If possible, use a thermoblock that fits a 5 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube; otherwise use a 2 mL LoBind tube.

steps.title: Resuspend cell pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 400 µL PBS and transfer the suspension to a 5 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube.

steps.title: Prepare nuclei lysis master mix
steps.instruction: Premix 400 µL Nuclei Prep Buffer, 400 µL Nuclei Lysis Buffer and 40 µL Proteinase K (kit reagents); vortex briefly. Make a master mix if processing multiple samples.

steps.title: Add lysis mix to cells
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL Premix Solution to the resuspended cells and mix by inverting the tube 10 times.

steps.title: Lysis incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate on the thermomixer at 56 °C, shaking at 700 rpm for 10 min.

steps.title: Add RNase A
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL RNase A, mix by careful pipetting 5 times with a wide‑bore P1000 tip, then invert‑mix the tube 5–10 times.

steps.title: RNase incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate on the thermomixer at 56 °C for another 10 min; because of high viscosity, invert the tube periodically if needed.

steps.title: Add precipitation enhancer
steps.instruction: After lysis, add 300 µL Precipitation Enhancer and mix by inverting 10 times. If using a 2 mL tube, split the lysate into two tubes and halve all reagent volumes for the subsequent steps.

steps.title: Add capture beads
steps.instruction: Using clean forceps, add 3 Capture beads (3 mm borosilicate glass beads) to a 5 mL tube (the third bead is a ‘sacrificed’ bead that will settle at the bottom). If using a 2 mL tube, add 2 beads per tube.

steps.title: Add isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 1.1 mL isopropanol to the tube.

steps.title: Bind DNA to beads
steps.instruction: Slowly manually invert the tube until DNA binds to the beads and no further compaction is observed (≈25–30 inversions). Alternatively, place the tube in a vertical rotating mixer at 9 rpm, room temperature, for 5 min.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the DNA‑bound beads.

steps.title: First bead wash
steps.instruction: Wash the beads with 750 µL Monarch Wash Buffer, gently invert 2–3 times, then discard the wash buffer.

steps.title: Second bead wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash with another 750 µL Monarch Wash Buffer, invert 2–3 times, and discard the buffer.

steps.title: Final bead handling
steps.instruction: Transfer the beads (with residual wash) into the Monarch Bead retainer sitting in a Monarch Collection tube. Pulse‑spin briefly (as short as possible) to remove remaining liquid; if DNA appears loose, omit the spin and absorb residual liquid with lint‑free tissue/Kimwipes. Air‑dry the beads for ~5 seconds.

steps.title: Prepare elution buffer
steps.instruction: Pre‑aliquot 500 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 9.0 into a clean 2 mL LoBind tube (this buffer can be replaced by Elution Buffer II from the Monarch kit or EEB from the ULK114 kit).

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Immediately pour the DNA‑bound beads into the tube containing the 500 µL Tris‑HCl buffer. If the previous steps were performed in two 2 mL tubes, combine all beads into this single elution volume.

steps.title: Elution incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate on the thermomixer at 56 °C for 10 min; optional shaking at 300 rpm can aid homogenisation of very viscous UHMW DNA.

steps.title: Dry bead retainer
steps.instruction: While the elution proceeds, place the bead retainer back into the collection tube and spin in a mini‑centrifuge for a few seconds to dry it. Remove the collection tube and transfer the dried retainer to a new 2 mL LoBind tube.

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: After incubation, pour the beads with the eluate into the bead retainer now sitting in the new 2 mL tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge to release DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 min. If DNA threads are still visible, centrifuge an additional minute at maximal speed.

steps.title: Adjust eluate volume
steps.instruction: Add 260 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 9.0 and pipette the eluate up‑and‑down 5–10 times with a wide‑bore tip for homogenisation. If the DNA remains too viscous, add an extra 300–400 µL Tris‑HCl to dilute and homogenise.

steps.title: Overnight incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples at room temperature overnight while rotating vertically at 9 rpm.

steps.title: Quantify extracted DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity using Nanodrop (or another spectrophotometer) by sampling three points (top, middle, bottom). Calculate %CV; if ≥ 100 % homogenise by repeated pipetting or rotation at 9 rpm for several hours up to overnight.

steps.title: Dilute DNA to target concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute or prepare the DNA so that its concentration is 20–40 ng/µL in a 2 mL tube. Mix well, incubate at room temperature, then cool on ice. Standard UL library prep requires 750 µL DNA; if the concentration of this volume is ≥ 50 ng/µL, dilute with 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 9.0 to a final volume of 900 µL.

steps.title: Prepare FRA dilution
steps.instruction:
Based on the DNA volume, prepare the FRA (transposase) dilution as follows:
- For 750 µL DNA: add 244 µL FDB and 6 µL FRA to reach 1 mL total.
- For 900 µL DNA: add 294 µL FDB and 6 µL FRA to reach 1.2 mL total.
(Values taken from the provided table.)

steps.title: Add FRA to DNA
steps.instruction: Mix the diluted FRA by quick vortexing, keep the tube on ice, then add the diluted FRA to the DNA. Stir while expelling the FRA with the pipette tip, then gently pipette with a wide‑bore tip 25–30 times to ensure a homogeneous, cold mixture.

steps.title: Incubate transposase reaction
steps.instruction:
Incubate the mixture as follows:
- Room temperature, rotating at 9 rpm for 10 min.
- 75 °C for 10 min.
- On ice for 2 min.

steps.title: Add rapid adapter (RA)
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL Rapid Adapter to each sample using a regular pipette tip; mix with a wide‑bore tip and visually confirm thorough mixing.

steps.title: Final incubation before loading
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature while rotating at 9 rpm for 30 min in a vertical rotator.

steps.title: Prepare priming mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the priming mix as described in the ONT ULK114 protocol using FCF and FTU.

steps.title: Quantify library DNA
steps.instruction: Quantify 2–3 µL of the library using the Qubit DNA BR kit (fluorometric) or Nanodrop (spectrophotometric). Optionally assess quality with Agilent TapeStation (genomic DNA protocol) to obtain a DIN value.

steps.title: Prepare loading mixture
steps.instruction:
For three loadings, mix the following in a 2 mL tube:
- 100 µL Sequencing Buffer (SBU)
- 10 µL Loading Solution (LSU)
- 90 µL UL library
Total volume = 200 µL. For additional loadings, reduce library volume by 10 µL each time (90, 80, 70, 60 µL) and adjust with 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 9.0 accordingly.

steps.title: Load library onto flowcell
steps.instruction: Load the prepared library onto the flow cell and allow tethering for at least 30 min (preferably 1 h) before starting the run.

steps.title: Select sequencing script
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate UL sequencing script in the ONT software based on the sequencing kit, ensuring the ‘long winding down’ setting is enabled before each mux scan.

steps.title: Flush flowcell periodically
steps.instruction: Flush the flowcell after every 20–24 h or when active pores drop below 1 000 (PromethION) using the Flow Cell Wash Kit (EXP‑WSH004). Follow ONT’s protocol for library recovery before flushing; recovered library can undergo another Nemo clean‑up before re‑loading.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality (optional)
steps.instruction: When possible, analyse extracted DNA by visual methods such as regular agarose gel electrophoresis, pulsed‑field gel electrophoresis (e.g., Pippin Pulse), Agilent Bioanalyzer, or Agilent TapeStation to inspect molecule length distribution.

steps.title: Quantify DNA for library prep
steps.instruction: Sample 9 µL DNA from the top, middle, and bottom of the solution, combine in a 2 mL tube, and quantify using both Qubit (fluorometric) and Nanodrop (spectrophotometric). Use a cut P10 tip; if the sample is viscous, cut the DNA thread by pushing the tip against the tube bottom. A positive‑displacement pipette may be used for higher accuracy.

steps.title: Add glass bead and vortex
steps.instruction: Add a glass bead (4 mm Monarch kit bead or 3 mm FindingNemo bead) to the DNA sample and pulse‑vortex at full speed (≈2400 rpm) for 1 min.

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Quantify DNA using the Qubit kit with Jurkat genomic DNA as the standard; if unavailable, use the kit’s lambda DNA standard. Use Nanodrop values to average the quantifications.

steps.title: Optional RNA carry‑over check
steps.instruction: Quantify any RNA carry‑over with the Qubit RNA Broad Range kit (optional). RNA should be < 50 % of the DNA concentration; if RNA > 100 % of DNA, adjust DNA input (add more DNA) or repeat RNase A treatment and glass‑bead precipitation.

steps.title: Alcohol‑free library purification (Nemo)
steps.instruction: Add 3 clean 3 mm borosilicate glass beads to the library in a 2 mL tube. Add 1 mL (1:1 volume) of 10 mM Hexamminecobalt(III) Chloride (CoHex) (for a 900 µL DNA input, total reaction volume becomes 1.2 mL; add 850–900 µL CoHex until the tube is full).

steps.title: CoHex incubation
steps.instruction: Rotate the tube on a vertical rotator at 9 rpm for 3–5 min (or hand‑invert 25–30 times, each full cycle ≈5 s). Then invert the tube 3 additional times by hand to ensure DNA precipitation onto the beads.

steps.title: Discard supernatant after CoHex
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the DNA‑bound beads.

steps.title: PEGW wash #1
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL PEGW buffer, gently invert 2–3 times, and incubate at room temperature for 3 min.

steps.title: Discard PEGW wash #1
steps.instruction: Discard most of the wash buffer, taking care not to disturb the DNA precipitate.

steps.title: PEGW wash #2
steps.instruction: Repeat the wash with 500 µL PEGW buffer, invert gently, then discard the supernatant (leaving a small dead volume).

steps.title: Final spin and buffer removal
steps.instruction: Pulse‑spin for 1 s in a mini‑centrifuge (or the shortest possible spin) to collect residual wash buffer; remove remaining traces with a fine pipette tip.

steps.title: Transfer beads to elution tube
steps.instruction: Quickly pour the DNA‑bound beads into a new 2 mL tube pre‑aliquoted with 300 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 9.0 (or ELU from the ULK114 kit). Do not let the beads dry.

steps.title: Elution incubation (Nemo)
steps.instruction: Incubate the library at 37 °C for 30 min, mixing every 10 min by gently aspirating and dispensing the eluate over the beads with a wide‑bore P200 tip.

steps.title: Bead retainer centrifugation
steps.instruction: Insert a bead retainer into a clean 2 mL tube, pour the beads from the previous step into the retainer, and centrifuge at 10 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 min.

steps.title: Post‑elution incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube for at least 30 min at room temperature with regular pipette mixing.

steps.title: Store or load library
steps.instruction: Store the purified library at 4 °C or proceed to loading onto the flow cell.
